description: Sealed transfer evaluation set for public Jimmer 0.12.2 skills

cases.prompt: In Java, our catalog has Product(id, sku, title, price) and a staging table ProductPriceImport(sku, price). Build a typed mutation that selects rows from staging where imported price is non-null and then inserts new products or updates existing products matched by sku. It must run as one database-side operation, set title to a fixed value for newly created rows, and return the affected product ids and skus.
assertions: Uses Jimmer's typed insert/upsert-from-select command rather than loading staging rows into Java.
The source is a typed query/base query with the non-null price predicate and maps sku and price into the target columns.
The conflict/matching key is sku and the update behavior changes price while insert behavior supplies the required title.
Uses a returning form (or an equivalent supported result mechanism) that returns the affected product ids and skus.

cases.prompt: A Kotlin inventory service receives an immutable StockItem(id, warehouseId, productId, quantity, version) command. Existing rows must be updated only when the supplied version matches; a missing id is an error, and a duplicate warehouseId/productId pair must not create a second row. Show the entity mapping and the save call, including the behavior the service should expect when the version check fails.
assertions: Maps the entity id, version property, and warehouse/product uniqueness needed by the stated persistence rules.
Chooses an update-only save mode (or an equivalent explicit update operation) so a missing id is not silently inserted.
Preserves optimistic-lock checking and explains that a stale version produces Jimmer's optimistic-lock failure rather than an overwrite.
Does not rely on an application-side existence check to enforce the unique pair; it uses a database/entity key constraint.

cases.prompt: For a Java travel API, query published Trip objects by destination and departure date. The response needs trip id/name, destination name, and each itinerary stop's city and arrival time, but must not load internal notes or the full hotel object. Keep filtering in SQL and make the returned graph explicit.
assertions: Builds a typed predicate for published trips, destination, and departure-date filtering instead of filtering the result list in Java.
Uses a Fetcher or equivalent explicit fetch graph selecting only the requested trip, destination, and stop scalar fields.
Does not include internal notes or an unrestricted hotel association in the fetch graph.
Executes the query through the Jimmer SQL client/repository with the shaped graph attached to the entity query.

cases.prompt: В Kotlin-приложении музея нужен входной DTO для создания Exhibition: обязательны title и museumId, дата открытия может быть задана, а server-managed id и createdAt нельзя принимать от клиента. Нужен также read DTO с id, title, museum name и количеством экспонатов, без самих экспонатов. Покажите DTO-описания и способ их использования в сохранении и запросе.
assertions: Defines a Jimmer input DTO whose writable properties are title, museumId, and optional opening date, excluding id and createdAt from client input.
Defines a separate output view/projection containing exhibition id/title, museum name, and an exhibit count rather than the exhibit collection.
Uses generated Kotlin DTO/input APIs in the save and query flow instead of accepting an arbitrary map or exposing the entity as the request body.
The count is computed by the database query/projection and does not require loading every exhibit into application memory.

cases.prompt: A Spring catalog service reads Product with its Category frequently and writes products through Jimmer. Configure transparent entity/association caching with Caffeine as a local first level and Redis as a shared second level, then explain what must happen to cache entries after a Jimmer update. Do not add manual cache reads to every repository method.
assertions: Configures a Jimmer CacheFactory (or the documented equivalent) with local and shared cache implementations rather than hand-written repository caches.
Includes entity and association cache handling sufficient for Product and its Category association.
States that Jimmer CRUD mutations invalidate affected cached data through its cache/transaction mechanism.
Keeps cache provider wiring centralized in configuration and does not claim that arbitrary out-of-band SQL is automatically observable without CDC/invalidation integration.

cases.prompt: A museum dashboard must show the 20 most visited exhibits in a date range, with visit counts and museum names. The current proposal loads all Visit rows and sorts them in Java. Recommend and sketch the Jimmer solution, including pagination and the aggregate ordering. If a database view or native SQL is not necessary, avoid it.
assertions: Uses a typed Jimmer query with grouping/count aggregation and orders by the count in the database.
Applies the date-range predicate before aggregation and limits the result to 20 through query pagination/limit.
Selects the exhibit identity/name and museum name alongside the aggregate count in a suitable tuple/projection.
Explicitly avoids loading all Visit entities or introducing native SQL/database views when the typed Jimmer query expresses the requirement.

cases.prompt: Add a nullable two-letter countryCode to TravelDestination and enforce uniqueness of (countryCode, name) for non-deleted destinations. Existing rows may have null countryCode. Provide the entity mapping and a safe PostgreSQL migration, including the index/constraint choice and how the nullable values behave.
assertions: Adds the nullable countryCode property with a length/column definition compatible with two-letter values.
Adds a database uniqueness rule for countryCode plus name that permits multiple rows whose countryCode is null, as PostgreSQL semantics require or via an explicit partial strategy.
Scopes uniqueness to non-deleted rows using the project's stated soft-delete condition rather than constraining deleted history.
The migration is additive and safe for existing rows by allowing nulls and creates the needed index/constraint before relying on the entity mapping.

cases.prompt: In a Quarkus Kotlin inventory service, expose a repository method that finds a warehouse by code and optionally accepts a caller-selected fetch shape for its bins and current stock summaries. Keep the method declarative, preserve not-found semantics, and show the Quarkus/Jimmer repository placement rather than putting SQL in a resource class.
assertions: Places the method in a Jimmer repository/repository abstraction recognized by the Quarkus integration, not in the HTTP resource.
Uses the warehouse code as a typed repository predicate and preserves a clear nullable/optional result for not found.
Accepts and applies a Fetcher for the warehouse graph so bins and stock summaries are caller-selected rather than always eagerly loaded.
Uses Quarkus CDI/Jimmer integration and does not embed hand-written SQL in the resource or repository method body.
